summary: Hancock County, Tennessee, lookout registered 2015 as US 1088; a 2008 visit found most cab glass and the cab floor gone, the first run of stairs removed, and it was not staffed. No build date in sources.

events.note: Visit report dated May 4, 2008: most cab glass and cab floor gone, first set of stairs removed, steel sound, cab needs paint, fence around the tower
Registered January 3, 2015 as US 1088, TN 24; nominated by Jeff Flanary

evidence.supports: cab glass, cab floor and first run of stairs gone
evidence.quote: Most glass is gone from cab, cab floor is also gone, stairs look in good shape however the first run has been removed.
Steel looks good, cab needs paint as there is some rust and grafitti.
has a fence all the way around it
Overall it is in good shape

evidence.supports: one other tower next to the fire tower, also a small weather station
evidence.quote: One other tower located next to the fire tower, also a small weather station.

evidence.supports: neighbouring weather station and tower with dish and antennas
evidence.quote: The tower has one dish and several vertical antennas mounted on its sides and cab.

evidence.supports: Sneedville elevation 2572 ft on Landforms list
listed as standing in Hancock County
most TDF towers built late 1940s to about 1960
evidence.quote: the majority of the TDF's fire lookout towers were constructed during the period between the late 1940s and ca. 1960

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register gives 2,559 ft (780 m) and the Landforms list gives 2,572 ft for the same Hancock County tower. The story reports the Register figure, which matches the record's 780 m, and notes the Landforms figure beside it.

sources.title: Tennessee Division of Forestry Fire Lookout Towers
sources.publisher: National Register of Historic Places multiple property document, National Park Service (npgallery.nps.gov)

notes_for_editor: The Register's Sneedville page does not name an administering agency. The brief lists the Tennessee Division of Forestry, and the Landforms list gives a Division-style code (1-12), but neither page says so outright; the story does not name the agency. No build date, design, height, or fire history was found. The only visit report is from 2008 and is 18 years old; current condition is unknown. The Register's visit form records the nominator as the 2008 visitor. A search snippet pointed to an easternuslookouts.weebly.com Sneedville page with a Division of Forestry District 1 heading, but the fetched copy did not show it, so it is not used.
